Extract information from pain drawing objects

Source: R/pdr_get_info.R
pdr_get_info.Rd

Extracts metadata or variables from a pdr_list (see pdr_match()), e.g. the list-column pdr_data. Simple elements (such as ".id" or ".timestamp") are returned as a vector, whereas the nested elements .points, .strokes, .polygons, .rgba and .stencil are returned as a list with one element per pdr_drawing.

Usage

pdr_get_info(pdr_list, id1 = ".id", id2 = NULL)

Arguments

pdr_list

A pdr_list (see pdr_match()), e.g. the pdr_data column of a pdr_tibble.

id1

A string specifying which element of each pdr_drawing to get. Default ".id".

id2

Optional string naming a column within id1 (when id1 is a tibble such as .points or .strokes) to extract.

Value

If id2 is NULL and id1 is one of .points, .strokes, .polygons, .rgba or .stencil: a list of the same length as pdr_list, with the element from each drawing. If id2 is NULL and id1 is any other element: a vector of the same length as pdr_list. If id2 is given: the column id2 of id1 for each drawing, as a list with one element per drawing (simplified to a vector only if every drawing contributes exactly one value).

See also

pdr_match()

Examples

# Extract ids (a vector)
pdr_example_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = pdr_get_info(pdr_data, ".id"))
#> # A tibble: 50 × 6
#>    id                               pdr_data          sex     age duration  pain
#>    <chr>                            <list>            <fct> <dbl> <fct>    <dbl>

#>  3 25062ac7dbeb08d8b532ac474a7849ca <named list [10]> Fema…  38.4 Acute        5
#>  4 0dc657fa6ed70150f9596fe692f2f9a0 <named list [10]> Male   98   Subacute     3
#>  5 fb61c33ffa09270a5c7931813e9d2d71 <named list [10]> Fema…  58.3 Acute        1
#>  6 328d31503202db3e5c1b8e78f287810e <named list [10]> Male   68.9 Subacute     7
#>  7 e07d8d7e7034ba3ae7f907de022af58d <named list [10]> Fema…  67.4 Subacute     6
#>  8 9996f1a95c8e939c6ab6258bfc76f722 <named list [10]> Fema…  53.4 Chronic      9

#> 10 0bcfd36a71b799e857f13c29011d21ff <named list [10]> Fema…  34.9 Subacute     4

# Extract the .x coordinates from the .points tibbles (a list)
pdr_example_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(x_coord = pdr_get_info(pdr_data, ".points", ".x"))
